nodes.summary: For a finite abelian group $A$, written additively, the $4$-rank of $A$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the quotient $2A / 4A$, where $2A = \{2a : a \in A\}$ and $4A = \{4a : a \in A\}$; it is the $2^j$-rank of $A$ for $j = 2$.
nodes.title: The $4$-rank of a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: For an abelian group $A$, written additively, and a natural number $j$, this is the quotient group $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$, where $2^kA$ denotes the subgroup $\{2^k a : a \in A\}$ and $2^jA \subseteq 2^{j-1}A$. For $j = 0$, where $j - 1$ is read as $0$, it is the trivial quotient $A / A$.
nodes.title: The two-power layer $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite abelian group, written additively, and let $j \ge 1$ be an integer. Writing $2^kA$ for the subgroup $\{2^k a : a \in A\}$, the $2^j$-rank of $A$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the quotient $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$, which is an $\mathbb{F}_2$-vector space because $2$ kills it.
nodes.title: The $2^j$-rank of a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: For an abelian group $A$, written additively, and a natural number $k$, $2^kA$ is the subgroup $\{2^k a : a \in A\}$ of $A$, the image of multiplication by $2^k$.
nodes.title: The subgroup $2^kA$
